page.layout: One page of text in a single main column; marginal notes in the left margin (three notes: "Assidua ebrietatis effectacer tissima.", "Crapula quid & unde?") and a short note "Galen-" at the lower right of the text block. Running head at top: "De Vita". Page number 618 at top left.

main_text.p: isti verbis egregie simulant, sed ebrietas, &c quae illam necessario consequuntur, turpitudo, ignominia, sanitatis viriumque corporis labefactatio, tremor, grauedo, pallor, linguae titubatio, contentio extremitatum in neruis, torpor, vtplurimum vero resolutio. Et certe constat quotidiana experientia, plærosque acrium illorum potatorum hoc tantum spectare, vt illos, quos vel amicitiae, vel honoris specie, atq; simulatione ad immoderate bibendum inuitant, atq; cogunt, cunctis deridendos propinentatq; comedendos, vt metaphoricos Terentius in Eunucho dixit, vt ita in totum dixisse liceat, nihil esse tam vtile, laudabile atque honestum, quod non deformet abusus hominum; quis enim non videt quotidie, antiquam illam propinandi consuetudinem ac philothesian amoris per se amicitiaeque plenam, proindeque honestam, iam a multis seculis in turpissimum flagitiosissimumque abusum degenerasse, & ad Plutonis vsque Cancellos ipsos Christianos hodie sibi inuicem specioso amoris atque amicitiae obtentu propinare. Atq; hinc promanasse putatur vox crapula, quae pro ebrietate metonymicos vsurpatur, cum tamen proprie sit ebrietatis effectus capitis nimirum lucta, agitatioque, cum sc. ex temulentia caput aggrauatur & tremit.

page.notes: Left margin notes: "Assidua ebrietatis effectacer tissima." (beside first lines); "Crapula quid & unde?" (beside the paragraph on crapula). Several words in the body are rendered with uncertain letters, e.g. "Eunucho", "philothesian", "Cancellos". The catchword "Gale-" stands at the foot right; it is treated as the start of the next page's word, shown as text here.
